schemes.label: Partita IVA

provenance.sourceText: «2. La fattura contiene le seguenti indicazioni: [...] d) numero di partita IVA del soggetto cedente o prestatore».

schemes.notes: DPR 26 ottobre 1972, n. 633, art. 21, comma 2, lettera d). Read directly at normattiva.it (https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.del.presidente.della.repubblica:1972-10-26;633~art21!vig=, plain HTTP response headed "vigente al 13/09/2026", curl with a browser User-Agent, no JS rendering needed), 2026-09-13. This binds the SELLER only ("cedente o prestatore") and carries no carve-out anywhere in comma 2 — a flat-rate/forfettario trader still holds and must state a Partita IVA. Cross-checked against the simplified-invoice regime at art. 21-bis, comma 1, lettera d) (same method/date, https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.del.presidente.della.repubblica:1972-10-26;633~art21bis!vig=): the seller's Partita IVA is NOT among the elements a simplified invoice (<=EUR100, raised to <=EUR400) may omit. Also cross-checked against the FatturaPA technical specification's own introduction, which restates the DPR 633/1972 list including "numero di partita IVA del cedente/prestatore" with no qualifier. For the SELLER this is genuinely unconditional — no VAT-regime carve-out exists. `required` is nonetheless set to `false` here, and this is the one deliberate departure from simply transcribing the seller's own unconditional rule: this catalog's ONLY axis is `appliesTo` (COMPANY/INDIVIDUAL/BOTH — the PARTY's own record type), and `resolveRequiredIdentifiers` takes no notion of transactional role at all. The exact same per-country array is read by `onboarding.tsx`/`company.settings.tsx` (always `partyType: "COMPANY"`, for the ACTIVE company about to issue invoices — i.e. always the SELLER in this product's outbound flow) AND by `client-upsert.tsx` (partyType taken from the CLIENT's own record type — i.e. the BUYER of that company's invoices). Setting `required: true` here would therefore ALSO become a hard block on saving an Italian, company-type CLIENT record — confirmed by reading client-upsert.tsx's `onSubmit` (a `required` scheme with an empty value calls `form.setError(...)` and `return`s, refusing to save) — but the BUYER-side rule is genuinely CONDITIONAL (DPR 633/1972 art. 21, comma 2, lettera f) — see this file's own LEGAL_ID entry below for the quote and the reasoning), not unconditional like the seller's. There is no per-role `required` in this schema, and the DB itself only allows one row per (countryCode, scheme) — `CountryIdentifierRequirement`'s unique key is `countryCode_scheme` — so a second "VAT" fact scoped to the buyer could not even coexist with this one; the seed would just overwrite it. `required: false` at country level is the same discipline this catalog already applies in fr.json/pt.json when a rule that IS mandatory for most sellers depends on a variable the catalog does not carry per party (there, the seller's own VAT regime; here, the party's ROLE in the transaction) — never a UI default, an explicit and documented choice. `appliesTo: 'COMPANY'` is similarly a simplification: an individual professional/sole trader acting as a business (an INDIVIDUAL record in this app) also holds and must state a Partita IVA when acting as a taxable person under this same lettera d) — but this choice is moot for the seller path specifically, because `onboarding.tsx`/`company.settings.tsx` always query `partyType: "COMPANY"` regardless of the active company's real legal form, so this fact is shown there unconditionally either way; it only affects whether an INDIVIDUAL-typed CLIENT also sees this field (optionally, since `required` is false here). FORMAT: the commonly-cited 11-digit numeric format for Partita IVA was NOT found in either DPR 633/1972 art. 21 or the FatturaPA Specifiche tecniche v1.4 (whose own `IdCodice` field states only a generic 28-character ceiling shared with foreign identifiers) — no `pattern` is declared here for that reason, the same discipline pt.json already applies to its own undeclared NIF/NIPC pattern.

schemes.label: Codice Fiscale

provenance.resolutionNote: Italian law does not always ask a buyer for the same document. A business buyer gives their VAT number (their Italian Partita IVA, or — if they are a business established elsewhere in the EU — their own country's VAT number instead). A buyer who is NOT acting as a business — typically a private individual — gives their Italian tax code (Codice Fiscale) instead of a VAT number. Right now this app has no way to tell those two situations apart for a given client: it only records whether a client is filed as a "Company" or an "Individual", and that is not the same thing as whether the client is acting as a VAT-registered business — an individual can run a business (and would then need to give a VAT number, not a tax code), and some companies are not VAT-registered (and would then need to give a tax code instead). Until a client record can say which of the two applies, this app cannot safely make either the VAT number or the Codice Fiscale mandatory here: doing so would sometimes ask a private individual for a business VAT number they will never have, or let a business through with neither number recorded. What would settle this: letting a client record say whether it is acting as a VAT-registered business, separately from whether it is filed as a Company or an Individual — once that exists, the correct one of the two identifiers can be safely required.

schemes.notes: DPR 633/1972, art. 21, comma 2, lettera f) (same page/method/date as the VAT entry above, 2026-09-13): the lettering repeats in the retrieved text — an "e)" covers the buyer's name/domicile and a first "f)" restates it, then a further "f)" (quoted here, semicolon-separated within the same point) states the actual number rule — quoted exactly as normattiva.it renders it, not tidied: «f) ditta, denominazione o ragione sociale, nome e cognome, residenza o domicilio del soggetto cessionario o committente, del rappresentante fiscale nonché ubicazione della stabile organizzazione per i soggetti non residenti; f) numero di partita IVA del soggetto cessionario o committente ovvero, in caso di soggetto passivo stabilito in un altro Stato membro dell'Unione europea, numero di identificazione IVA attribuito dallo Stato membro di stabilimento; nel caso in cui il cessionario o committente residente o domiciliato nel territorio dello Stato non agisce nell'esercizio d'impresa, arte o professione, codice fiscale;» Precisely: an Italian-established taxable-person buyer gives Partita IVA; a taxable person established in another EU Member State gives THEIR OWN state's VAT id, not an Italian Partita IVA; a buyer resident/domiciled in Italy who does NOT act in the exercise of a business, art or profession gives Codice Fiscale instead. Cross-validated by a second, independent primary source, the FatturaPA technical specification's own `CessionarioCommittente` block, which states the same alternative structurally: «IdFiscaleIVA (la valorizzazione di questi elementi è in alternativa non esclusiva a quella dell'elemento CodiceFiscale; in altri termini, possono non essere valorizzati se è valorizzato l'elemento CodiceFiscale; [...]) [...] CodiceFiscale: la valorizzazione di questo elemento è in alternativa non esclusiva a quella dell'elemento IdFiscaleIVA (può non essere valorizzato se è valorizzato l'elemento IdFiscaleIVA); consente l'inserimento del numero di codice fiscale del cessionario/committente.» (same PDF/URL as this file's VAT entry's own IT-3-equivalent citation — see this file's top-level `notes`). Also cross-validated by the simplified-invoice regime, art. 21-bis comma 1 lettera e): a simplified invoice can reduce the buyer's identification to "il solo codice fiscale o il numero di partita IVA" for an Italy-established buyer, the same CF/VAT alternative. `appliesTo: 'BOTH'` and `required: false` are both deliberate: BOTH because either a COMPANY-record or an INDIVIDUAL-record buyer can legally need either identifier depending on taxable-person status, not on record type (an INDIVIDUAL freelancer needs Partita IVA exactly like a COMPANY; a COMPANY-record entity that is not a taxable person would need Codice Fiscale exactly like a private INDIVIDUAL) — `appliesTo` cannot express that finer axis, so BOTH is the least wrong choice, not a claim that record type decides anything here. `required: false` because the rule is a genuine either/or conditioned on taxable-person status, which this catalog does not track per party (see this fact's own `resolutionNote`) — setting it `true` under either scheme name would demand a document some lawful buyers do not have. `provenance.kind` is `unverified` here NOT because the underlying law is in doubt (it is fully quoted above, read directly at normattiva.it) but because — per this task's own instructions — a fact this well-established in law but not yet safely enforceable by this product (the deciding variable, taxable-person status, exists nowhere in this app's data model) is recorded as `unverified` with a `resolutionNote` naming what the product would need, rather than graded `legal` with a `required` value that cannot honestly reflect a role-dependent rule. FORMAT: Codice Fiscale length IS established as 11-16 alphanumeric characters (Specifiche tecniche v1.4, §3.3.1, `DatiAnagraficiCedenteType`: «CodiceFiscale (Rif. par. 3.2): formato alfanumerico; lunghezza compresa tra 11 e 16 caratteri.», repeated identically for `RappresentanteFiscale` and `CessionarioCommittente`) — no `pattern` is declared on this fact regardless, by the same all-or-nothing discipline de.json's own VAT entry already uses (an unsourced claim elsewhere in the same fact keeps the whole fact from being promoted); if this fact is ever promoted, `^.{11,16}$` is the primary-sourced pattern to use.

notes: Italy (2026-09-13). Two schemes, both graded conservatively (`required: false`) for the SAME structural reason spelled out in each fact's own `notes`: this catalog's `appliesTo` axis (COMPANY/INDIVIDUAL/BOTH, a PARTY-TYPE distinction) is consumed identically by the SELLER path (`onboarding.tsx`/`company.settings.tsx`, always `partyType: "COMPANY"` for the active company) and the BUYER path (`client-upsert.tsx`, `partyType` from the client's own record type) with NO role axis anywhere in `IdentifierSchemeFact`, `CountryIdentifierRequirementsFile`, the `CountryIdentifierRequirement` Prisma model, or `resolveRequiredIdentifiers`'s own signature — confirmed by reading all four. `required: true` is enforced as a REAL, hard save-block (not merely a UI hint) in all three consuming screens' own `onSubmit`/validation code (client-upsert.tsx, onboarding.tsx, company.settings.tsx all call `form.setError(...)` and refuse to save when a `required` scheme's value is empty). Italy's SELLER-side rule (Partita IVA, DPR 633/1972 art. 21 comma 2 lettera d) IS unconditional — no carve-out exists for any seller entitled to issue an Italian VAT invoice at all. Italy's BUYER-side rule (same article, lettera f) is NOT unconditional — it depends on whether the buyer is a taxable person (Partita IVA / an EU state's own VAT id) or not (Codice Fiscale instead), a distinction this catalog's PartyType axis does not carry. Because the schema cannot scope a fact to the seller call-site only, and because the DB enforces exactly one row per (countryCode, scheme) — so a second, buyer-scoped fact under the SAME scheme name could not coexist with a seller-scoped one — `required: true` for either scheme would inevitably ALSO hard-block a lawful Italian buyer/client record that this research does NOT establish as needing that exact identifier. Both facts are therefore kept `required: false`, each fully explaining the true, asymmetric legal position in its own `notes`/`resolutionNote` rather than encoding a boolean that cannot honestly represent both roles at once. DELIBERATELY NOT ENCODED, reported instead (see this task's own report for the full reasoning): the Codice Destinatario / PEC (SdI routing identifier of the recipient, 6 or 7 alphanumeric characters depending on whether the recipient is a Pubblica Amministrazione, with '0000000' and 'XXXXXXX' as documented placeholder values) and the PA's own Codice Ufficio (IndicePA registry) are established by the FatturaPA Specifiche tecniche v1.4 (an implementing technical measure, traced through D.Lgs. 127/2015 art. 1 and DM 55/2013 Allegato A), NOT by DPR 633/1972's own invoice-content article — a full-text search of the retrieved art. 21/21-bis for "Codice Destinatario"/"PEC"/"SdI"/"Sistema di Interscambio" found zero genuine matches. This is also structurally transmission/routing data (which delivery channel to use), not a party-identity fact in the sense this catalog otherwise models (Partita IVA, Codice Fiscale) — and it already has a home elsewhere in this repository: `b2g-routing/data/it.json` already declares an "IT_PA_CODE" (Codice Univoco Ufficio) requirement for GOVERNMENT clients specifically, sourced to the SAME Specifiche tecniche, and `formats/national/fatturapa-provider.ts` already reads/validates a 7-character "IT_SDI" party identifier via `isValidSdiCode` (`/^[A-Za-z0-9]{7}$/`) for the ordinary B2B/private case — confirmed by grepping this repository before writing this file, not merely assumed from the research notes. Adding a THIRD scheme here would also be a breaking change with no frontend `data-cy` target (schema.ts's own header).
